description.value: This study examined associations between weight-related eating behaviors assessed with the Weight-Related Eating Questionnaire and brain activation during food-related go/nogo fMRI tasks.

spans.text: Using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), this study measured brain activation in regions of interest across impulsive, reflective, and interoceptive circuitry.

value: We hypothesized that the HGo vs. LGo contrast would be associated with the emotional eating and external eating subscales because both of these measures are related to eating as a reward-driven behavior.

Additionally, we hypothesized that the HGo vs. LGo contrast would be associated with routine and compensatory restraint because brain regions related to inhibition and self-control would be recruited to compensate for reward salience in individuals who exercise greater restraint in eating.

We hypothesized that the HGo vs. HNogo contrast would be associated with routine and compensatory restraint scores because restrained eating requires exercising inhibition in response to high-calorie foods.

We also hypothesized that the HGo vs. HNogo contrast would be associated with higher emotional eating and external eating because individuals with higher scores in these subscales have greater attraction than inhibition in response to high-calorie foods.
